meta.disclaimer: DARK-WEB INTEL, NOT DARK-WEB ACCESS. OSTARA does not run Tor and does not fetch .onion sites directly. This registry documents the dark-web-adjacent sources the /api/darkweb endpoints query from clearnet: Ahmia (Tor search engine, clearnet-accessible) and ransom.privtools.eu (ransomware leak-site monitoring, sourced from ransomware.live). Ransomware victim listings are OPERATOR CLAIMS, not verified breaches — leak-site posts are written by the attackers and may be exaggerated, misattributed, or fabricated. Never treat a listing as proof of compromise; verify independently before acting. OSTARA never fetches, hosts, or displays stolen data content.
meta.title: Dark-web intel sources registry

sources.access: clearnet HTTPS, no key, no Tor required
sources.name: Ahmia
sources.notes: Search engine for Tor hidden services, accessible from clearnet at ahmia.fi. OSTARA queries its HTML search results (no documented JSON API). Results are unvetted onion-site listings; relevance ranking is Ahmia's own. Bot protection may block datacenter IPs — the endpoint degrades honestly when blocked.

sources.access: clearnet HTTPS, no key — JSON dump of recent 30 days
sources.name: ransom.privtools.eu (ransomware victim dataset)
sources.notes: JSON dataset published by ransom.privtools.eu, sourced from ransomware.live's leak-site monitoring (hundreds of .onion leak sites). The ransomware.live v2 API blocks datacenter IPs via Cloudflare, so this mirror is used instead. Credit ransomware.live as the original source. Listings are operator claims, NOT verified breaches.

sources.access: clearnet HTTPS, browsable free; wider API needs free Observer key
sources.coverage: Ransomware operators, victim disclosures, blacklisted wallets, zero-days
sources.name: Darkfield (Orizon)
sources.notes: Public observatory over ransomware leak-site data. Free JSON feed / REST / RSS with attribution. Not yet wired into an endpoint — listed here as a verified fallback source if ransomware.live is unreachable. API base: darkfield.orizon.one.

sources.access: requires Tor; not queried by OSTARA
sources.name: Ransomware leak sites (.onion)
sources.notes: The groups' own Tor hidden services are the primary source. OSTARA does not run Tor and never fetches these directly — they are listed here so analysts know what the aggregators above are mirroring. Do not invent onion URLs; they rotate frequently.
